faults.quote: Is that structure MECE — what overlaps, and what's missing? And which branch would you prioritize first, and why?
faults.why: Several distinct questions are stacked into one opening turn: MECE, overlaps, gaps, priority and rationale.

faults.quote: I'll come back to average fare in each year shortly.
faults.why: The candidate asked for the network average fare in each year. No ledger item holds it, yet it was deferred and never refused. It later resurfaced only as Lakeport-specific fare data.

faults.quote: On Hub-Lakeport average one-way fare in each year: we'll get there in a bit.
faults.why: This is a second deferral that renames the earlier network-fare ask as a Lakeport fare the candidate never asked about. It reads as dangling narration.

faults.quote: An exhibit for you — Hub–Lakeport — Economics of one one-way flight, FY2023 vs. FY2025 ($).
faults.why: The candidate asked only about competitor entry and pricing. The Lakeport per-flight exhibit was handed over unrequested.

faults.quote: what would you want to understand about why Larkspur's fares fell?
faults.why: This asks why fares fell immediately after releasing the line that explains it (Larkspur matched the competitor's fares), and it is bundled with a second question.

faults.quote: Now, an exhibit: Proposed new routes — Planning estimates (average per flight across Hub–Ashford and Hub–Brookhaven).
faults.why: The candidate had asked about load factor and passenger mix and had never raised exiting routes or adding new ones. Pushing the new-routes exhibit hands over the solution path.

faults.quote: Hub–Port Avery shows the same pattern: 80 seats, a 75% load factor and $20 of extras per passenger, with variable cost of $11,000 per flight in both years, while the average fare fell from $240 to $160.
faults.why: Port Avery per-flight economics were released without any ask.

faults.quote: As the exhibit shows: A Hub–Lakeport flight has 80 seats and there are 2,000 of them a year, and the load factor was 75% in both FY2023 and FY2025.
faults.why: The candidate asked whether load factor or passenger mix (business-heavy) had shifted. Only the load factor already on screen was repeated, with no 'I don't have' for passenger mix.

faults.quote: Earlier you said "× $200 - $9,200 = $400 per flight, so $1.4M, and we'd be roughly breakeven"
faults.why: The quote is clipped and starts mid-expression ('× $200'), so it reads wrong.

faults.quote: Then tell me the single biggest risk to your recommendation.
faults.why: The candidate had just listed risks in the recommendation (the unproven $180 fare and an entrant attacking a third route). This re-asks the risk stage, bundled with a math probe.

faults.quote: If you had to guard against that, how would you do it?
faults.why: The candidate's last answer already gave a mitigation ('I'd pilot one route first').
